attributes.body_ja:
名詞（めいし）の「ため」（漢字（かんじ）では「為（ため）」）は、目的（もくてき）を表（あらわ）すときに使（つか）われます。「ため」は、それだけで使（つか）うことはできません。必（かなら）ず目的（もくてき）を表（あらわ）す、ほかの言葉（ことば）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。「ため」のあとには、(A) が目的（もくてき）だとはっきりと示（しめ）すために、格助詞（かくじょし）の「に」が付（つ）くことも多（おお）いです。

しかし、「ために」が動詞（どうし）の過去形（かこけい）に付（つ）くと、原因（げんいん）や理由（りゆう）を表（あらわ）すことが多（おお）くなります。この場合（ばあい）、(A) が主（おも）な原因（げんいん）・理由（りゆう）となって (B) が起（お）こったことを表（あらわ）します。

この「ために」を使（つか）うときは、動詞（どうし）の過去形（かこけい）、「の」が付（つ）いた名詞（めいし）、または連体形（れんたいけい）のイ形容詞（けいようし）やナ形容詞（けいようし）のあとに「ために」を続（つづ）けます。

「ために」は、形（かたち）は同（おな）じでも、文脈（ぶんみゃく）や、一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）う言葉（ことば）によって、過去（かこ）の出来事（できごと）の原因（げんいん）や理由（りゆう）を表（あらわ）したり、先（さき）に学（まな）んだように、行動（こうどう）の目的（もくてき）を表（あらわ）したりと、意味（いみ）が変（か）わります。
attributes.body:
ため (or 為（ため） in its kanji form) is a noun in Japanese that can be translated quite closely to 'sake' in English. However, it is classified as a non-independent word in Japanese, and must always be connected to another word which illustrates the 'sake' that ため is highlighting. The case marking particle に will often be added after ため, to show that (A) is a goal that something will be done to reach.

However, when used with verbs in the past tense, ために more frequently highlights that something happened 'due to (A)', rather than 'for the sake of (A)'. Because of this, a more accurate description of ため in all situations is 'in light of (A)'. This expresses that (A) is the primary or major event/thing that resulted in (B).

To use ために as 'in light of', 'as a result of', or 'because of', attach it to the end of verb in its past form, or a noun follow by の. It may also be used after い-Adjectives or な-Adjectives in their attributive form.

This 'in light of (A)' nuance can be used in reference to things that have already happened (as above), or in reference to something that is considered as the purpose of an action (as in our other ために grammar point).

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: ため vs により (によって)

attributes.body: Both can express cause, but with different perspectives. ために often reflects the speaker's point of view, e.g. 試合は台風のために中止になった ('The game was canceled in light of the typhoon.') によって typically conveys an external or objective cause, e.g. 台風によって多くの家が壊れた ('Many houses were damaged due to the typhoon.')

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

second_relatable.title: によって・による
second_relatable.meaning: By means of, According to, Depending on, Because of, Due to

attributes.body: Both relate cause and result, but their structures are different. ゆえに can be used as a sentence-level connector meaning ‘therefore’, drawing a conclusion a stated reason, as in 予算が不足している。ゆえに延期した (‘The budget was insufficient; therefore, it was postponed.’). ために is a grammatical form meaning ‘because of' or 'due to’ comes within a sentence to similarly express purpose, e.g. 雨のために試合が中止になった (‘The game was canceled due to the rain.’).

attributes.body: ために and せいで can both mean 'due to (A)', but with a difference in tone. せいで almost always implies a negative or undesirable result. ために can be used with either positive or negative nuance. Also, ために can mean 'for the purpose of (A)', which せいで cannot.

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

attributes.body: ために and せいで can both express the idea of 'due to (A)', but they differ in that おかげで almost always describes a desirable result, while ために can be used with either a positive or negative nuance. ために can also, in some cases, mean 'for the purpose of (A)', while おかげで cannot be used in this way.

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

attributes.body: そのため(に) can be seen as a more specific version of ために. ために follows a noun, verb, or adjective phrase to express purpose or reason. そのため(に) appears at the beginning of a sentence and means 'due to that' or 'in order to do that', referring back to what was previously said.

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

second_relatable.title: そのため(に)
second_relatable.meaning: For that reason, Because of that, To that end

attributes.body: Both ために and につき can express 'due to (A)', but differ in tone and usage. ために requires の to connect to nouns, e.g. 悪天候のため ('Due to bad weather') につき connects directly and sounds stiffer or more formal, e.g. 悪天候につき (Same meaning) Unlike ために, につき cannot be used to express purpose.

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

second_relatable.title: につき
second_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

attributes.body: ために and その結果 both express a cause/effect relationship, but in different ways. ために is used within a sentence following a noun, verb, or adjective, and can mean either 'due to (A)' or 'in order to (A)'. その結果 comes at the beginning of a sentence and always means 'as a result of that', referring back to the previous statement.

first_relatable.title: ために
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Because of, As a result of

attributes.body: Both express reason or cause, but with different constraints. ために connects to nouns with の and means 'due to (A)' or 'for the purpose of (A)'. にあって attaches directly to a noun and is limited to situations, positions, or conditions, e.g. 非常時にあって ('in a state of emergency') It cannot be used with general nouns the way ために can.
